title: Long MU — Q3 FY2026 Beat-and-Raise Event at Correct Entry (~$1,125)
entry: Enter $1,094–1,140 (MU at ~$1,125 June 22 morning; ATH $1,149.43 logged June 18). Scale: 1/3 position at current levels on June 22; add 1/3 only if DXY confirms close below 100.00 this session (regime gate cleared); hold final 1/3 in reserve for any post-earnings pullback to $1,080–1,100 if report delivers a beat but stock fades intraday on profit-taking. Do NOT initiate above $1,150 — at that level pre-earnings premium is excessive relative to Target 1 ($1,200). Replaces long-mu-q3-earnings-june24-event-2026-06-19 which was created with incorrect price data from the June 19 briefing.
stop_loss: $1,018 daily close (~9% below $1,117 midpoint) — implies MU Q3 revenue guidance for Q4 cut below $31B, signaling HBM demand has peaked earlier than expected; OR NVDA Annual Meeting June 24 delivers explicit demand-softening language from Jensen ('monitoring inventory levels,' 'digestion period'); OR DXY fails to clear 100.00 by June 24 AND 30Y breaches 5.00% simultaneously (macro regime turns actively hostile to semis longs); OR SK Hynix or Samsung announces a significant HBM3E capacity increase that would erode MU's pricing power within two quarters
targets: $1,200 — RBC Capital raised PT to $1,200 post-ATH; MU Q3 beats consensus ($34.5B+, GM 82%+, EPS $19.50+); sell-side upgrade cycle begins as ~15 Hold-rated analysts face re-rating pressure; +7.4% from $1,117 midpoint; take 40% of position

$1,300 — Wedbush raised PT to $1,300 citing 20%+ DRAM/NAND price rises; Q4 guidance implies $35.5B+; HBM supply deficits confirmed into mid-2027; full re-rating from cyclical discount to quality-growth multiple; +16.4%; take 40%

$1,450 — blue sky: AI supercycle memory re-rating; MU valued at ~9× forward EPS on $160+ annualized trajectory, implying market credits sustained 80%+ gross margin baseline through FY2027; +29.8%; hold remaining 20% through next earnings if quarterly data sustains thesis
catalyst: Micron Q3 FY2026 earnings June 24 after market close. Consensus: $34.66B revenue / $19.95 EPS (TradingKey). Management guided record $33.5B revenue with ~81% gross margin and $19.15 EPS. Analysts at RBC (PT $1,200) and Wedbush (PT $1,300) raised targets in the June 20–22 pre-earnings window citing 20%+ DRAM/NAND price increases and HBM fully booked through 2026. MU hit an all-time high of $1,149.43 on June 18, 2026 — up ~300% YTD. The same session as earnings, NVIDIA Annual Meeting (9 AM PT virtual) has Jensen Huang addressing AI demand trajectory, Taiwan $150B commitments, and the $25B debt offering rationale. Two major AI-hardware catalyst events on June 24 create maximum volatility and upside optionality for the AI memory complex. SK Hynix HBM4E sample delivery confirmation provides additional read-through: if the next-generation product is also oversubscribed before launch, memory pricing power remains with suppliers through at least mid-2027.
thesis:
Micron Q3 FY2026 arrives with the company having guided record revenue of $33.5B — driven by AI infrastructure and HBM demand that has structurally decoupled MU from the traditional DRAM commodity cycle. The AI capex confirmation cascade is extensive: NVDA's $25B bond offering generating $85B in orders, AMD 57% YoY data center revenue growth in Q1, and every major hyperscaler reiterating or increasing compute capital expenditures for 2026. NVIDIA's Blackwell architecture requires approximately 8× HBM3E per GPU module, creating dedicated HBM demand that scales directly with every GPU sold into data centers. Micron's ATH of $1,149.43 on June 18 reflects markets beginning — but not finishing — the re-rating from cyclical memory supplier to structural AI infrastructure provider.

The gross margin trajectory is the re-rating catalyst the market has not fully credited. Management guided ~81% gross margin for Q3 — comparable to Qualcomm at peak. Memory companies historically trade at cyclical discounts because margins swing from 10% to 60%+ with supply/demand cycles. At 81%, MU is demonstrating something the market has not priced since before the 2022 downcycle: HBM supply is capacity-constrained, and pricing power has shifted structurally from buyers (cloud hyperscalers) to suppliers (MU and SK Hynix). If Q3 confirms 81%+ and Q4 guidance implies sustained margins above 80%, the sell-side upgrade cycle accelerates — with approximately 15 analysts still rated Hold on MU and only a few at Buy, the upgrade is mathematical pressure, not speculation.

The June 24 double event — MU earnings after close AND NVDA Annual Meeting at 9 AM PT — creates a compounding catalyst window. Jensen Huang's comments on AI demand, Taiwan production, and post-$25B-debt infrastructure plans will set the tone for the full AI hardware sector heading into MU's print. A constructive NVDA Annual Meeting raises all boats in the AI semis complex; a demand-softening signal at the NVDA meeting would be the worst-case scenario for MU shares even before the memory company reports. This is the primary reason the position is sized at 3% rather than 5% — the NVDA single-name event risk is embedded in the same trading day.

The counter-party is the memory bear who argues: (1) $1,125 per share prices in perpetual AI capex growth with no digestion cycle — historical memory supercycles peak and reverse within 12–18 months as customers absorb inventory; (2) MU at $1,125 is ~300% above its YoY level, pricing in years of earnings growth that has not yet been delivered; (3) SK Hynix's HBM4E sample confirmation means competition into H2 2026 is accelerating, potentially capping MU's pricing power into 2027. These are legitimate structural risks, which is why this is an event trade (1–2 week horizon) rather than a position trade, and the $1,018 stop reflects respect for the cyclical risk.
bull_case: MU reports Q3 revenue of $34.8B (beat by $1.3B), gross margin 82.5% (above 81% guide), EPS $20.15. Q4 guidance: $36.0B+, implying HBM demand acceleration with no inventory concern. NVDA Annual Meeting same day: Jensen reiterates '$200B+ AI infrastructure demand for calendar 2026' and names MU as a critical supply partner. Sell-side upgrades begin week of June 29: Goldman, Morgan Stanley, BofA all move from Hold to Buy. MU reaches $1,200 within 3 sessions post-June 24; $1,300 in 2-3 weeks.
bear_case: MU reports Q3 in-line ($33.5B) but Q4 guidance disappoints: $32.0B–$33.0B revenue and gross margin guiding to 78–79%, implying HBM pricing has plateaued. NVDA Annual Meeting Jensen notes 'we are monitoring inventory at certain cloud customers' — subtle softening signal. MU falls from $1,125 to $1,050–1,080 on the day-after reaction, approaching but not immediately triggering the $1,018 stop. Position held at 1/3 size pending Q4 guidance confirmation over the following 2 weeks.
invalidation: $1,018 daily close; OR MU Q3 gross margin guidance for Q4 below 78% (memory price plateau); OR NVDA Annual Meeting Jensen delivers explicit demand-softening language; OR DXY fails to clear 100.00 by June 24 AND 30Y breaches 5.00% simultaneously; OR SK Hynix or Samsung announces significant HBM3E capacity addition that would erode MU's pricing power within two quarters
